subject.title: Strict-agentic retry should allow terminal turns with only read-only inspection tools

question: Should planning-only terminal outcomes with only replay-safe/read-only tool activity get a same-model strict-agentic continuation retry, or should planning-only remain model-fallback-only?
rationale: Current code already has side-effect-aware replay metadata, but planning-only is an explicit harness classification routed to fallback; changing that behavior affects Codex/native harness terminal semantics and should be owner-approved before automation writes the fix.

options.title: Add bounded read-only planning retry
options.body: Use the existing replay-safe metadata boundary to retry planning-only terminal outcomes once or twice when only read-only inspection occurred, with Codex and embedded-runner tests.

options.title: Keep fallback-only semantics
options.body: Leave planning-only harness outcomes as model-fallback classifications and document that strict-agentic same-model retry only covers empty and reasoning-only turns.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Ask for a redacted consumer-path transcript before choosing retry semantics, accepting that the local patch cannot be retired yet.

recommendation.title: Add bounded read-only planning retry
recommendation.body: Use the existing replay-safe metadata boundary to retry planning-only terminal outcomes once or twice when only read-only inspection occurred, with Codex and embedded-runner tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest current-source owner signal for the touched Codex app-server and strict-agentic retry code paths.
